keyframe_review.note: 69,423 km2 for 1188-1219: Turov, Pinsk and the Pripyat basin (25.4-30.6 E, 51.0-53.5 N). The page gives no area, so nothing to compare. The same cells lie inside Cliopatria's Principality of Kiev shape to 1187; the page puts Turov's independence from Kievan Rus' in 1162 ('Finally in 1162 the principality was passed ... back to one of the Izyaslavichi') and a semi-independent Pinsk 'at the same time'. The shape is kept and the start is Cliopatria's 1188 to avoid double-drawing against the Kiev shape.

69,358 km2, 65 km2 less than 1188; no page dates a change in 1220. In 1223 'the army of Turau participated' at the Kalka River with Smolensk. In the early 13th century (no year) Turov became dependent on Galicia-Volhynia; the page does not date it.

Same area as 1220. The Mongol invasion page lists 'Turov and Pinsk' among the belligerents of 1237-1241 and says the principalities became Mongol vassals; it dates no event in Turov. Cliopatria ends the shape in 1240.

correction.text: the Turov-Pinsk land of 1240 carried forward: the principality kept its own princes through the Mongol decades (Yuri Volodymyrovich to 1292, Dmitry Yuryevich from 1292 in the page's list) and reappears in Cliopatria's 1294 rows of Turov and Pinsk

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1241-1293 although the Turov page says the principality 'enjoyed wide autonomy' under Galicia-Volhynia 'until the Mongol invasion' and joined Lithuania only in the early 14th century. The page's list of princes is partly garbled; the division into separate Turov and Pinsk rows from 1294 is Cliopatria's, not the page's.

The page is silent on 1188: it has Turov, 'the capital plus the town's immediate vicinity', pass in 1162 from the descendants of Yuri Dolgoruki back to Yury Yaroslavich, a grandson of Svyatopolk II, who 'gained full independence from Kievan Rus'', with a semi-independent Pinsk created at the same time.

notes:
START AND END. Cliopatria draws this land inside its Principality of Kiev shape until 1187 and as its own polity from 1188 to 1240; the Turov page puts full independence from Kievan Rus' in 1162 (the sentence names Yuri Dolgoruki as the giver in 1162 while the same page has Andrei and Boris, his descendants, holding Turov around the 1150s, so I could not reconcile it from this page). The dossier starts at Cliopatria's 1188 to avoid double-drawing against the Kiev shape; if the Kiev dossier ends Turov's cells in 1162 this dossier can start there with the 1188 shape carried back. The found event is confidence 1 for that reason.

THREE ROWS, ONE LINE. Cliopatria's 'Principality of Turov and Pinsk' (1188-1240) and the 1294-1325 rows 'Principality of Turov' and 'Principality of Pinsk' share Wikidata Q671362; the 1294 rows cover 270 of the 274 cells of this dossier's last shape, so they are the same land. The brief's rule (one dossier under the earlier slug with all Names) would claim rows that belong to batch eu-16-f, which owns principality-of-pinsk and principality-of-turov; their files are not edited here. This dossier keeps its own Name only and hands over to them in 1293/1294; the 1241-1293 gap is filled by a new keyframe, because the page shows the principality alive and ruled by its own princes then. If eu-16-f merges those two rows into one dossier, successors here should point at it.

NOT DRAWN. The page says Turov became dependent on Galicia-Volhynia in the early 13th century (no year) and kept wide autonomy 'until the Mongol invasion'; with no year the vassal relation is not recorded (it would be a vassal_start in the principality-of-galicia-volhynia dossier). The Mongol suzerainty over all the Rus' principalities after 1240 (Mongol invasion page: vassals, tribute 'until well into the 14th century') belongs to the Mongol Empire / Golden Horde dossiers.

PAGE BUDGET 2 of 2 used (Principality of Turov; Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'). Neither page gives an area, so the Cliopatria area (69,423 km2) could not be compared. The page's list of princes is partly garbled, so no ruler strip is given.

WebFetch returns a model's summary of each page, not the page text: wording in quotation marks in this dossier is the summary's rendering of the page's sentence, verbatim only where the summary itself quoted it; the dates and names are the summary's.
